findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as a query parameter
findings.actual: The API requires the key to be sent in the X-API-Key request header, and rejects query parameters with a 401 status
findings.how_found: Made a request to /v1/listings using the documented query parameter and read the 401 error detail
findings.impact: All requests fail until authentication is moved to headers

findings.documented: Every listing_id is globally unique, and each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property
findings.actual: The endpoint returns massive numbers of duplicate properties masquerading under different listing_ids (only 50 unique properties found out of 4850 records)
findings.how_found: Calculated unique properties by checking latitude, longitude, and apartment details across the full dataset
findings.impact: Frontend applications will display identical listings to users repeatedly if not deduplicated locally

findings.documented: Money conventions dictate Indian rupees, integer, everywhere in the API
findings.actual: The price_min and price_max fields return decimals representing Crores (e.g., 12.44), not integer Rupees
findings.how_found: Calculated the costliest project and observed a decimal value that is physically impossible for integer Rupees
findings.impact: Frontend applications will display apartments as costing $0.15 instead of millions if the unit is assumed to be raw rupees

findings.documented: Endpoints GET, POST, and DELETE /v1/favourites are documented for saving listings.
findings.actual: The server returns a 404 Not Found for all requests to /v1/favourites, indicating the endpoint is completely missing/unimplemented on the backend.
findings.how_found: Attempted to use the save feature in the UI and observed 404 Vercel edge errors in the network tab.
findings.impact: Users are completely unable to save, view, or remove favourite listings because the server rejects the documented routes.
